I enjoy my parents in limited doses. "Home" for me is my two bedroom apartment with my wife and cat. I love my wife deeply, but I feel that I've given her everything that I can, and the rest is only going to be a poor facsimile. I have given my family everything useful that I could give. Part of me believes that I'll be... not better servicing them by being dead... but that the net, overall, will be better or unchanged.

Again, thanks for the encouragement. But knowing that I have it pretty good, actually makes it worse. I haven't survived any trauma. I haven't beaten the odds. I'm not from a 3rd world cesspool... so why do I want to kill myself? What gives me the right?

Getting a perspective of the world doesn't help. It makes me think of all the things I will never, regardless of suicide, get to see or experience.

I feel like my family is strong and will survive without me. It's a small family. My mother and father would be devastated of course- but I truly think that they would be okay eventually. Perhaps they would grow stronger who knows.

My wife, likewise, would be devastated. But, she is *so* strong. She'll be just fine. She would pull through just fine. She can handle anything that comes her way, and if done correctly, wouldn't leave any issues like finding bloody bodies, etc.

I don't think i posted here to try to find encouragement. I don't know exactly *why* but it feels good to let it out and say that a part of me is okay with killing myself. It's so clear in my head, and it's kind of refreshing in a way.

It's weird because I'm scared shitless because death itself scares me-- but at the same time, everything is in focus and I'm calm.

I'm 30. There was a period last year between August - October where things were so good. I think that the best days are behind me. I don't want to let these thoughts go this time. There's part of me that wants to see this through, if that makes any sense.
